headline: 5 Dividend Stocks Yielding Up to 8% That Could Keep Paying for Years
summary: A 52-year raise streak sounds safe until you put it next to a 7.8% yield, a reset dividend, and a consumer staples giant whose payouts free cash flow still covers even as profits shrink. Five income stocks, five very different kinds of durability.

headline: General Mills vs. Hershey: Which Dividend Stock Pays You More in 10 Years?
What Is Going On With PepsiCo Stock?
summary: PepsiCo (PEP) stock trades at 16.1 times earnings. The median S&P 500 company, by contrast, trades at 22.8 times earnings. Over the past year, PepsiCo shares lost 11.9%, while the S&P 500 returned 17.9%. This underperformance occurred even as the company posted higher sales, margins, and cash flow in the twelve months to September 5, 2026. The market is either overlooking an improving business, or accurately pricing a company with stalled growth. What does a buyer get at this price.

headline: Two Food Giants Yield Over 7%. Only One Has the Cash to Back It Up
summary: General Mills and Kraft Heinz both hand income investors a yield above 7%, but the cash sitting behind those payouts tells two very different stories about which quarterly check is actually safe.

headline: 1 Safe-and-Steady Stock on Our Buy List and 2 We Brush Off
summary: Stability is great, but low-volatility stocks may struggle to deliver market-beating returns over time as they sometimes underperform during bull markets.
